title: Stamp Coupling (Interservice Over-fetching)
pattern: An interservice RPC, network call, or system call requests a massive compound data contract structure when the recipient only reads a tiny subset of the returned properties.
why_bad: It wastes massive network bandwidth and CPU cycles serializing/deserializing unused fields. It also couples the downstream service to changes in unused attributes of the upstream contract.
detection: RPC call invocations where the deserialized response type contains properties that are never used in the caller project.
counterexample: Standard database integrations where reading full rows is optimized by index lookups and does not traverse network boundaries.
source: Mark Richards & Neal Ford, *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* (2020), Chapter 9 ("Stamp Coupling").
